candidates.change_summary: Delete the statement `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` so the public getter never reflects the call.
Replace the assignment `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.number;` so the public getter returns the block number instead of the timestamp.
Move the assignment `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` to the top of the function body so it executes even when a subsequent require reverts, changing the observable value after a failed call.
Remove the requirement that msg.value equals 10 ether, so calls with any value (including zero) are accepted.
Remove the one-call-per-block timestamp check so multiple calls in the same block are accepted.
Remove the update of pastBlockTime so the timestamp check never blocks subsequent calls.
Change the payout condition from block.number % 15 == 0 to block.number % 15 != 0, inverting when the refund occurs.
Change the payout condition modulo from 15 to 7, changing which block numbers trigger the refund.
Delete the entire conditional refund block so the contract never pays out.
Replace the require for msg.value with a stricter check of 20 ether, rejecting the original 10-ether calls.
Delete the statement 'pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;' so pastBlockTime is never updated.
Replace 'pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;' with 'pastBlockTime = block.number;' so pastBlockTime records the block number instead of the timestamp.
Delete the statement 'require(msg.value == 10 ether);' so calls with any value can succeed and update pastBlockTime.
Remove the statement that updates pastBlockTime, so the state variable never changes.
Assign block.number instead of block.timestamp to pastBlockTime, producing a different stored value.
Assign block.timestamp - 1 instead of block.timestamp so the stored value differs by one second.
Delete the statement `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` so pastBlockTime is never updated.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.number;` so the stored value differs.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp + 1;` so the stored value is incremented.
Delete the statement `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` so the public getter keeps returning the stale old value after a call.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.number;` so the stored value is the block number instead of the timestamp.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp + 1;` so the stored timestamp is one second ahead of the original.
Delete the statement `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` so the state variable is never updated after a call.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp + 1;` so the stored value differs from the original after any successful call.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` with `pastBlockTime = block.number;` so the stored value is the block number instead of the timestamp.
Change the value check from equality to inequality so calls with any value other than 10 ether succeed.
Remove the requirement that the timestamp must exceed pastBlockTime, allowing multiple calls in the same block.
Remove the update of pastBlockTime so the timestamp guard never blocks subsequent calls.
Invert the block-number condition so the payout occurs on every block not divisible by 15.
Remove the transfer statement so the contract never pays out the balance.
Change the timestamp guard from strictly greater to greater-or-equal, allowing two calls within the same block timestamp.
